explanatory_strength.rationale: Inversion works: AMD's moat is stable (x86 server franchise + second-source GPU), not impregnable against CUDA and custom silicon. Segment economics and owner cash are hard to fake; the premium is the fragile part.

evidence_sufficiency.rationale: Packet supports decision-grade component math and FY2025 cash facts. Gaps: empty management_facts, no Instinct SKU margin series, adversarial lint still notes prior classification IRR drift in dive text.

downside_control.rationale: Partial dhando fails at this price. Spot embeds AI dreams; contract low/base (~$69–$96/sh) shows how much capital can be lost without any solvency event. Invert: what if we are wrong about share gains?

return_vs_alternatives.rationale: Negative expected returns at $549.86 under both Lawrence (-14.56%) and contract (-22%) mean opportunity cost versus almost any other idea in the universe. Do not rationalize with narrative.

claims.claim: Proof-first component math sums to about $96 per share versus about $550 market, so the debate is premium for AI share-gain optionality when cash-flow math is deeply negative at spot.
Lawrence synthesis base case is -14.56% per year over seven years on $3.37 starting free cash flow per share at $549.86.

strongest_counter_explanation: Circle of competence says semiconductor cycles look expensive at peaks; this time AI demand is structural and AMD's second-source role permanently re-rates cash multiples upward.
most_important_missing_fact: Independent evidence that Instinct software/ecosystem can sustain pricing power against CUDA without perpetual gross-margin giveaways.
falsifiers: Two consecutive quarters of Data Center revenue decline year over year

specialist_findings: Munger: invert the AI story. Stable moat does not justify destroying capital at 160x owner cash. Reject. Prefer contract capitalization over growth narrative.
